GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Corrects the previous scope mismatch: baseline GRACE documentation is not an implementation. The earlier baseline bundle was cancelled by the user; this change explicitly authorizes writing and testing the whole target Rust/Kotlin product from the current context files, with one final architecture and task-level parallelizable dependencies.

Alternatives.Alternative: Patching the already approved C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE plan to add source writes: rejected by GRACE 4 approved plan immutability and the mismatch with its defined documentation-only scope.
Creating a sequence of prototype applications and rewriting them afterward: rejected, the whole target architecture will be implemented directly.
Kotlin-only watch sender and Rust receiver: technically viable but duplicates core contract logic and violates the selected shared Rust design.
Running permanent Syncthing-like watch daemon: rejected for unacceptable idle resource usage.
Phone/cloud relay to compensate for hotspot client isolation: out of scope; topology must be diagnosed and reviewed.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Pin tested Android/Wear OS targetSdk/minSdk and Kotlin/Compose/Gradle/Rust toolchain compatibility from the local build environment before approving the executable plan.
Choose reviewed Rust PAKE and TLS crates with adequate support on Android ARM64 and Windows; user-confirmed one-time short code must use an offline-guess-resistant authenticated enrollment mechanism.
Validate Galaxy Watch Samsung Voice Recorder read access in a normal non-privileged APK. Android scoped storage and provider availability can vary by watch generation.
Validate S25 Ultra hotspot station-to-station TCP forwarding and multicast; manual IP does not override hotspot client isolation.

Define actual time and power budgets from measured physical trials, including idle drain and charging restrictions; candidate threshold is excess drain at most two percentage points over eight matched idle hours, subject to evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: User opens watch UI, connects to Wi-Fi hotspot, pairs with Windows, taps Send New; file arrives without original deletion or intermediate phone app.
Computer offline: discovery tries a bounded time, user sees clear status and watch network resources are promptly released; no overnight drain from retries.
Recording is 1 GiB and upload fails at 70 percent: next eligible session reconciles durable receiver ranges, sends only missing content and commits one verified file.
Receiver disk full or reboot halfway through a chunk: no acknowledgement of non-durable bytes and later reconciliation is safe.
Untrusted hotspot client guesses discovery address or pairing code: unauthenticated traffic is rejected with rate limits and no plaintext transfer.
Watch stops recording during transfer or content identity changes: abort/defer unstable content and preserve originals.
Wear OS removes foreground execution permission or imposes background restrictions: an explicit user-visible fallback and durable resume state are used; no hidden self-restarting service.
No hardware is accessible to CI: all code-build and host tests still run, while measured hardware release gates remain pending rather than fabricated.
